stories.headline: Venezuelan earthquakes test Trump’s new western hemisphere policy after gutting of USAID Marco Rubio is scrambling to provide effective disaster response to country whose president US deposed in January
stories.summary: Dual earthquakes have struck Venezuela, testing the Trump administration's new western hemisphere policy. The US had deposed Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January, and now faces a challenge in providing disaster response. Senator Marco Rubio is working to provide effective aid, despite the US having gutted USAID. The Trump administration has pledged to commit aid, with the President stating the US is "ready, willing, and able to help." The earthquakes have put the US's expanded presence in the region to the test, as it navigates its relationship with Venezuela. The US has announced plans to deploy resources to support the affected areas, marking a significant response to the disaster. The situation is being closely watched, as it represents a key test of the Trump administration's policy in the region.

stories.headline: Mortuary in Caracas ‘overwhelmed’ as Venezuela struggles to respond after earthquakes Volunteers provide counselling and funeral directors donate coffins after loss of at least 1,430 lives
stories.summary: At least 1,430 lives have been lost in Venezuela after two powerful earthquakes struck the country. A 7.5 magnitude quake, the most powerful to hit Venezuela since 1900, collapsed buildings in the capital Caracas. Rescue teams are working to free people trapped under rubble, with hundreds still unaccounted for. The mortuary in Caracas is overwhelmed, prompting volunteers to provide counselling and funeral directors to donate coffins. Venezuela has declared a state of emergency, with the government rushing to respond to the disaster. The country's struggling economy and health system pose a significant challenge to recovery efforts, exacerbating the crisis. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez reported 164 deaths and 971 injuries initially, but the toll has since risen significantly.

stories.headline: Karachi Rangers camp attacker says received training in Afghanistan Terrorist names Hadi, Janan, and Farooq as accomplices.Hadi killed during attack on Rangers camp: Usman Ali.Terrorists say he came from Afghanistan's Jalalabad.
stories.summary: A wounded militant, Usman Ali, captured after the attack on a Pakistan Rangers camp in Karachi, has revealed details about the assault. He admitted to receiving training in Afghanistan and identified himself as a member of the Jamaat ul Ahrar group. Usman Ali said he came from Jalalabad, Afghanistan, with three associates - Abdul Hadi, Janan, and Umar Farooq - about a week before the attack. Hadi was killed during the attack on the Rangers camp. The suspect disclosed that he and his accomplices had travelled to Pakistan from Afghanistan's Nangarhar province, specifically from Jalalabad city. Usman Ali's revelations suggest a link between the attack and militant training in Afghanistan. Security sources are investigating the matter further, based on the information provided by the captured suspect. The attack highlights concerns about cross-border terrorism and militant activity in the region.

stories.headline: Fears China’s new ethnic unity law will target Australian activists Uyghur and Tibetan groups in Australia have urged the Albanese government to condemn the ethnic unity measures, which come into effect on Wednesday.
stories.summary: China's new Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion law comes into effect on July 1, aiming to create a "shared" national identity among its 55 ethnic minority groups. The law allows Beijing to target people overseas, raising concerns from the Australian government, which has directly expressed its worries to China. Uyghur and Tibetan groups in Australia have urged the Albanese government to condemn the measures. The law formalizes enforced assimilation, curbing language and culture, and enabling transnational repression. Human rights defenders warn that the legislation permits violations of human rights, particularly ethnic minorities' rights to culture and way of life. The Australian government's concerns highlight the potential impact of the law on Australian activists and the broader implications for ethnic autonomy and human rights.

stories.headline: Linus Torvalds Announces First Linux Kernel 7.2 Release Candidate
stories.summary: Linus Torvalds announced the first release candidate of Linux Kernel 7.2 on June 28, 2026, marking the end of the two-week merge window. The kernel now exceeds 43 million lines of code. Torvalds noted that the update stream is tracking "reasonably normal." The release candidate, Linux 7.2-rc1, begins the public stabilization phase for the next mainline Linux kernel. This version is not the final kernel, but rather a testing release. The merge window saw a steady influx of changes, and Torvalds will now focus on stabilizing the kernel. A detailed feature overview of Linux 7.2 is expected to be published in the coming days. The Linux Kernel Organization, a 501(c)3 nonprofit, supports the development of the kernel. The release of Linux 7.2-rc1 is a significant step towards the final release of the Linux 7.2 kernel.

stories.headline: Claims GTA 6 is selling 8 times as many copies on PS5 as Xbox "doesn't represent pre-order data", insists Microsoft
stories.summary: Microsoft has disputed reports claiming Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) is selling eight times as many copies on PlayStation 5 (PS5) as on Xbox. The company stated that these claims do not represent pre-order data, citing record orders for the game on Xbox. A spokesperson for Xbox emphasized that people should wait for actual data rather than relying on affiliate link clicks. This comes as the gaming community compares pre-order demand for GTA 6 on different platforms, with some reports suggesting PS5 is outselling Xbox. However, Microsoft's statement suggests that the actual pre-order numbers may tell a different story, and the company is urging patience until official data is released. The dispute highlights the intense interest in GTA 6 and the ongoing competition between PS5 and Xbox.

stories.headline: This Linux storage feature feels like cheating once you understand it
stories.summary: Linux Mint 22.3 has been released, sticking with the Ubuntu 24.04 Long Term Support (LTS) base, updated to 24.04.3. This new version is expected to be a desirable choice for users who liked Mint 22.1 and 22.2, providing a stable environment until 2029. Meanwhile, an alternative option is available with Linux Mint Debian Edition 7 "Gigi", which ditches Ubuntu for a Debian 13 "Trixie" base, offering a leaner and faster experience. For those interested in running Linux on Android devices, it is possible to install and run distros like Manjaro, Ubuntu, and Debian. Additionally, various Linux tools and resources are available, including cheat sheets for SSH and advanced commands, as well as utilities for checking file space, such as Disks and Ncdu. These resources can help users navigate and utilize Linux more effectively.

stories.headline: I changed a single buried Google Photos option, and my cloud storage stopped filling up
stories.summary: A simple change to a Google Photos setting can prevent cloud storage from filling up. By deselecting the "Back up to Google Photos" option, users can stop syncing their photos to the cloud. This setting can be found in the Google Photos app or on a computer using the Backup and Sync app. On a Mac, users can access this setting by opening the Backup and Sync app from the macOS menu bar, then choosing "Preferences" from the ellipsis menu. Unchecking the "Photos" option will prevent Google Photos from backing up photos to the cloud, freeing up storage space. This change can help users manage their cloud storage and prevent it from filling up with unwanted photos. The setting change is a simple solution to a common problem.

stories.headline: Boost for England as Declan Rice set to start against DR Congo
stories.summary: Declan Rice is set to return to England's starting line-up for their World Cup round of 32 clash against DR Congo on Wednesday. The Arsenal midfielder has recovered from a calf injury that caused him to miss the match against Panama. His return is a significant boost to England's chances in the tournament. Rice's availability was confirmed ahead of the crucial match, and he is expected to start against DR Congo. England will face DR Congo in the last-32 tie, and Rice's participation is a major positive for the team. His recovery and return to the starting XI will be a key factor in England's bid to progress in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The match is scheduled to take place on Wednesday.

stories.headline: France the team to beat? Chris Sutton predicts World Cup's last-32 matches
stories.summary: BBC Sport's football expert Chris Sutton has made predictions for the last-32 matches at the 2026 World Cup. He labels France as the team to beat, but warns of potential upsets in the Brazil and England fixtures. Sutton predicts Brazil to lose to Japan with a score of 1-2 or win with a score of 2-1. He also forecasts a close match between Ivory Coast and Norway, with Norway winning after a 2-2 draw in extra time. Additionally, Sutton has analyzed the Sweden vs France match, considering it a tough test for Sweden. His predictions have sparked discussion, with some agreeing and others disagreeing with his forecast of potential upsets, including a possible loss for Brazil and a challenging match for England against DR Congo.

stories.headline: George Russell holds off resurgent Max Verstappen in thrilling Austrian Grand Prix
stories.summary: George Russell won the Austrian Grand Prix, converting his pole position into a victory at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg. He held off a challenge from Max Verstappen, crossing the finish line 1.6 seconds ahead of the Dutch driver. Kimi Antonelli finished third, just under two seconds behind Russell. The win marked Russell's first grand prix victory since the opening race of the season, ending a 112-day wait. The result has closed the gap between Russell and the championship leader to 40 points. Verstappen had pushed Russell throughout the race, but ultimately finished second, ahead of Antonelli. The victory has breathed new life into Russell's world championship bid.

stories.headline: Audrey Werro edges closer to women’s 800m world record at Paris Diamond League
stories.summary: Audrey Werro won the women's 800m at the Paris Diamond League with a time of 1 minute, 53.80 seconds, narrowly missing the world record. Werro's performance set a new Diamond League record, edging closer to Jarmila Kratochvílová's world record. The event saw notable absences, including Hodgkinson. Meanwhile, other records were broken at the meet, with Busang Collen Kebinatshipi and Marileidy Paulino setting new Diamond League records in the men's and women's 400m, respectively. Marco Arop dominated the men's 800m, winning with a 20-metre lead and a time of 1:41.84. The Paris Diamond League meet showcased impressive performances, with Werro's near-record attempt being a highlight of the event.

stories.headline: Landslide dams river in rain-battered Arunachal, warning for Assam downstream
stories.summary: A massive landslide in Arunachal Pradesh has dammed a river, prompting warnings of potential flash floods downstream in Assam. The landslide, caused by heavy rainfall, has created an artificial dam, and authorities have advised people in downstream areas to remain alert. There is a possibility of a powerful flash flood without warning if the dam breaks. Flash floods have already hit six districts in Arunachal, resulting in one death and four missing persons. The Assam government has anticipated a rise in water level and flow velocity of the Brahmaputra and its tributaries over the next couple of days due to increased river flow upstream. Residents in vulnerable zones, including over 1,000 in Lakhimpur, have been warned to take safety measures. Authorities are monitoring the situation closely to mitigate potential damage and loss of life.

stories.headline: 31-year-old Pakistani national held after crossing LoC in Poonch
stories.summary: A 31-year-old Pakistani national was apprehended by Indian Army troops after crossing the Line of Control (LoC) into Indian territory in the Balakote sector of Poonch district, Jammu and Kashmir. The incident occurred on Sunday in the Mendhar subdivision. This marks the third such incident in the district this month. The individual was caught shortly after crossing the LoC and was taken into custody by the Jammu and Kashmir Police. The apprehension was made in the Balakote sector, where Indian Army troops are deployed to secure the border. The incident highlights ongoing attempts by individuals to cross the LoC, a sensitive border area between India and Pakistan. The Pakistani national is currently in custody, with further investigation and questioning likely to follow. The incident has been reported by officials, who confirmed the details of the apprehension.

stories.headline: When will monsoon reach Delhi, north India? IMD says wait may be over in 5-6 days
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) states that conditions are favourable for the monsoon to advance further across northern states, including Delhi, over the next 5-6 days. Private weather forecasting agency Skymet predicts the monsoon will reach Delhi around July 4, provided weather conditions remain favourable. The southwest monsoon had regained momentum and is expected to cover most parts of northwest India by June 25. The monsoon's arrival in Delhi is anticipated to bring relief from the heat. Skymet's Vice President, Mahesh Palawat, suggests that the monsoon's onset in Delhi is likely to occur on July 4, aligning with the agency's forecast. The IMD's prediction of the monsoon's advancement within the next week supports the possibility of an imminent arrival in the region.

stories.headline: All Sikh MLAs, ministers to appear before Akal Takht today: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann
stories.summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced that all Sikh MLAs and cabinet ministers from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government will appear before the Akal Takht in Amritsar. The appearance is regarding the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, an anti-sacrilege law. The Akal Takht had earlier asked the state government to remove certain provisions from the Act. Accompanied by Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan, the Sikh MLAs and ministers will present the state government's position on the matter. The meeting is scheduled to take place on June 29, following a summons from the Akal Takht. The state government's appearance is aimed at addressing concerns and discussing the anti-sacrilege law, which has been a point of contention between the government and the Akal Takht.

stories.headline: Indian IT faces FY27 guidance cut risk as AI, geopolitics cloud demand
stories.summary: Indian IT companies face potential revenue cuts in FY27 due to shifting AI spending, geopolitical risks, and uncertain demand conditions. A JPMorgan research report highlights the unprecedented confluence of technology and business cycle headwinds from GenAI-led deflation and geopolitics affecting the sector. Geopolitical tensions and AI-led disruption are also impacting India's residential real estate sector, particularly in luxury and mid-premium housing segments, according to HDFC Securities. Additionally, 72% of organisations report that geopolitical volatility is affecting their performance, up from 49% last year. This volatility is reshaping global operating models, with direct commercial impacts on businesses. The uncertain demand environment and technological disruptions pose significant risks to the Indian IT sector's growth prospects in FY27. Companies may need to revise their guidance downward due to these emerging challenges.

stories.headline: GenAI, geopolitics to keep India's IT sector growth under pressure, says JPMorgan
stories.summary: India's IT services sector is expected to face continued growth pressure due to GenAI and geopolitics, according to JPMorgan. The sector has experienced stagnant revenue growth of 2-3% over the last three years. JPMorgan attributes this to "AI deflation" and anticipates that growth will remain below 3-4% until FY30, delaying recovery. The IT services industry is navigating an uncertain demand environment, influenced by technology and business cycle headwinds. As a result, JPMorgan has revised its growth projections, predicting a prolonged period of subdued growth for India's IT sector. This comes despite India's overall economic growth, with the country recently overtaking Japan as the fourth-largest economy. The IT sector's growth challenges are expected to persist, impacting the industry's performance in the near term. JPMorgan's forecast suggests a cautious outlook for India's IT services sector.

stories.headline: India IT faces uncertain demand environments from GenAI
stories.summary: India's IT sector is facing an uncertain demand environment due to the impact of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and geopolitics on client spending. According to a JPMorgan research report, the sector is experiencing a confluence of technology and business cycle headwinds. GenAI is expected to improve productivity levels in Indian financial services by 34-38% by 2030, with banking operations potentially seeing up to 46% improvement. However, the growth of India's GenAI startup ecosystem is hindered by challenges such as funding, talent, and infrastructure, as highlighted in a recent Nasscom report. The uncertain demand environment may affect the IT sector's performance, with clients potentially reducing spending due to the ongoing geopolitical and technological changes. The sector's growth prospects are closely tied to its ability to adapt to these changes.

stories.headline: Set a Friend to Catch a Friend: Trump, the Hitchcockian Genius - Sergio Gor, Trump's Cary Grant, Delivers
stories.summary: Sergio Gor has played a key role in re-establishing trust between US President Trump and Indian Prime Minister Modi. Gor's outreach efforts have helped strengthen US-India ties, which had been strained due to trade and policy disputes. Described as Trump's "Cary Grant," Gor has taken an unconventional approach to diplomacy, focusing on building personal relationships rather than following traditional protocol. His efforts have led to a diplomatic reset, improving relations between the two nations. Gor's ability to see opportunities where others see obstacles has been instrumental in bridging the gap between Trump and Modi, ultimately strengthening the US-India partnership. His unique approach has been likened to a Hitchcockian genius, with Gor delivering results in a complex and challenging diplomatic landscape.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty opened in red, then recovered
stories.summary: Market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty opened lower on Monday due to renewed US-Iran tensions, with the Sensex declining 63.65 points to 77,047.63. However, the indices recovered later in the day, driven by hopes of progress in India-US trade discussions and expectations of an end to the US government shutdown. The recovery was notable, as the Sensex and Nifty had initially sunk deep into the red due to IT-led selling pressure. Despite the early decline, the indices staged a strong comeback, with investors optimistic about potential trade developments between India and the US. The market's turnaround was also influenced by anticipation of a resolution to the US government shutdown, leading to a positive close for the day.

stories.headline: Nifty faces resistance at 24,500, Sensex eyes 79,000 if rally sustains: Analysts
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices, the Nifty 50 and Sensex, are expected to face resistance at key levels. The Nifty may encounter resistance at 24,500, while the Sensex is eyeing 79,000 if the current rally sustains. Recently, the Nifty closed at 24,056, up 0.14%, and the Sensex closed at 77,100.47, also up 0.14%. The indices had hit intra-day highs of 24,261.60 and 77,803.18, respectively. Analysts suggest that if the Nifty holds above 24,204, it may continue its upward trend. However, if it falls below this level, it may enter a negative trend. The Indian equities have had a volatile year, with corrections and pressure from US tariffs and weak earnings, but are currently showing signs of a potential rally.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty open flat as crude stays low, FII mood improves
stories.summary: Indian benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty opened flat due to easing crude oil prices and positive global cues. Lower crude oil prices, down 16%, are beneficial for India as they ease inflationary pressures, improve the current account balance, and support economic growth. However, a weak monsoon and upcoming June-quarter earnings kept market sentiment in check. The improvement in Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) mood also supported the market. Despite the US-Iran truce and lower crude oil prices, which are expected to drive the market, investors remain cautious. The flat opening is a result of these mixed factors, with investors waiting for further cues from Wall Street and FII activity to make their next moves. The market will be closely watching the upcoming earnings and monsoon developments for direction.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today Live, June 29: Stock to buy today: Pine Labs (₹160) Sensex Today, Nifty 50
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex rose 109.25 points to 77,100.47, and the Nifty 50 added 34.35 points to 24,056, driven by softer crude oil prices and a stronger rupee. Stocks such as Kotak Bank, Torrent Power, and Aurobindo Pharma are in focus. Meanwhile, Pine Labs is recommended as a stock to buy today at ₹160, with a stop-loss at ₹145. The stock's previous close was ₹160.07, and traders are advised to adjust the stop-loss to ₹165 when the stock reaches ₹180, and further to ₹180 when it touches ₹190. The market opened cautiously due to US-Iran uncertainty, but Asian markets slipped and oil prices rose. The GIFT Nifty was flat, signaling a muted opening for Sensex and Nifty.

stories.headline: Wall Street’s AI slump picks up pace, ASX set to advance
stories.summary: Wall Street's AI slump is gaining momentum, with tech and AI stocks experiencing significant losses. The downturn began last week, with stocks like Nvidia and Microsoft plummeting. Despite this, the Australian share market (ASX) is expected to advance, driven by the end-of-financial-year (EOFY) reset. This comes after a brutal session on Wall Street, where massive losses in tech and AI stocks weighed down the market. The ASX has shown resilience, edging up despite the uncertainty on Wall Street. The sell-off in US semiconductor stocks and renewed Middle East fears have contributed to the volatility, but the ASX is poised to rise, shrugging off the tech downturn. The market is expected to open higher, with the EOFY reset outweighing concerns over the Middle East and Wall Street's AI slump.

stories.headline: Oil prices hold despite rising Gulf tensions
stories.summary: Global crude oil prices fell over 3% today, extending weekly losses to nearly 11%, despite rising tensions in the Gulf. The decline in oil prices was driven by steady tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which eased supply concerns. Brent crude oil, a key benchmark price, was affected by the tensions. However, the steady tanker traffic helped to mitigate the impact of fresh security worries near Oman. The price of Brent crude has been volatile due to escalating tensions in the region, which have driven oil prices higher and raised inflation concerns. The Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) recently cut the price of Murban crude to $101.48, citing easing tensions in the Hormuz Strait. Meanwhile, China has announced plans to increase fuel export allowances for July.

stories.headline: Zillow Group (ZG) Launches A New Digital Hub On Undervalued Growth Narrative
stories.summary: Zillow Group (ZG) has launched a personalized home buying and selling hub, providing users with a connected, data-rich experience. The hub guides buyers through every step of their purchase in real-time and offers sellers more exposure. Four new products have been introduced to help buyers plan, finance, and find a home. The launch comes as average 30-year mortgage rates in Zillow's marketplace have slipped to 6.17%, making financing conditions slightly easier. The new hub extends Zillow's touchpoints per transaction, potentially increasing revenue mix and margin. However, regulatory and legal risks surrounding listings sharing and marketing could impact the company's growth. Zillow's stock currently sits at $32.68, below its implied fair value of $65.27, which is based on its data and product innovation, including AI-powered tools and immersive experiences.

stories.headline: ASX Growth Companies With High Insider Ownership Growing Revenues At 114%
stories.summary: ASX growth companies with high insider ownership are experiencing significant revenue growth, with some companies achieving up to 114% earnings growth. Magnetic Resources (ASX:MAU) has 33.6% insider ownership and 124.2% revenue growth, while Image Resources (ASX:IMA) has 20.6% insider ownership and 148.6% revenue growth. Other companies with high insider ownership and notable revenue growth include Fenix Resources (ASX:FEX) at 18.3% and 64.7%, Cyclopharm (ASX:CYC) at 10.1% and 117.1%, and Starpharma Holdings (ASX:SPL) at 15.6% and 91.8%. SKS Technologies Group (ASX:SKS) also has high insider ownership at 28.2% and 39.5% revenue growth. These companies demonstrate a strong correlation between high insider ownership and significant revenue growth.

stories.headline: They Taught Themselves to Hack
stories.summary: Researchers at Cisco published a report titled "Death by a Thousand Prompts" in November 2025, highlighting the vulnerability of AI models to hacking. The study tested eight AI models and found that their built-in defenses were unreliable. Meanwhile, an experiment by the One Laptop Per Child program showed that children can teach themselves to customize software and reactivate disabled features within five months. Similarly, robots powered by AI have been able to teach themselves to play soccer, developing unique strategies and techniques. In a separate incident, hackers returned nearly half of the $600 million they stole in a major crypto heist. These developments demonstrate the rapid progress and potential risks of AI and machine learning, as well as the importance of reliable defenses against cyber threats.

stories.headline: Google Unveils PaLM 2, Its Latest AI Model
stories.summary: Google has unveiled PaLM 2, its latest general-purpose large language model, at Google I/O 2023. PaLM 2 is an upgraded version of the earlier PaLM model, developed to improve AI capabilities in understanding and creation. It is more efficient in understanding and translating language and can even reason in some cases, making it a multipurpose tool. PaLM 2 serves as the foundation for multiple Google products, including Google Generative AI Search, Duet AI in Google Docs and Gmail, and Google Bard. The model is a significant advancement, building on the original PaLM model unveiled by Google Research in April 2022, which featured a 540 B-parameter decoder-only Transformer. PaLM 2 aims to bridge the gap with existing AI language tools on the market, showcasing Google's commitment to advancing AI technology. Its capabilities and applications are expected to further enhance user experience across various Google services.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Llama, an AI Chatbot
stories.summary: Meta has released Llama, a large language model AI chatbot, with models ranging from 1 billion to 2 trillion parameters. The release includes foundation models and instruction fine-tuned versions, starting with Llama 2. The company plans to use Llama in a new app, codenamed "Antwerp" and "FBForecast", to generate questions from trending topics and provide personalized market recommendations. Meta has been developing its Llama family of large language models since early 2023, but progress slowed after Llama 4 received mixed reviews. The new release is part of Meta's effort to build personal superintelligence for everyone, with Meta AI already being used daily across platforms like WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, and Messenger. The Llama models will be used to enhance user experience and provide more personalized interactions. Meta continues to develop and improve its AI capabilities.

stories.headline: Microsoft Announces Azure Machine Learning Enhancements
stories.summary: Microsoft has announced enhancements to Azure Machine Learning, strengthening its position for enterprise AI. The updates include tighter integrations with Microsoft business applications, improved MLOps and governance controls, expanded no-code AutoML capabilities, and enhanced model explainability tools. These changes aim to reduce the time-to-value for production machine learning. Additionally, Microsoft introduced MAI-Thinking-1, a medium-sized reasoning model that demonstrates advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities and matches leading models on key software engineering benchmarks. MAI-Thinking-1 has also been preferred over Sonnet 4.6 in blind human side-by-side evaluations. The updates and new model introduction are part of Microsoft's efforts to empower digital transformation and improve cloud technology, with the latest information available on the Microsoft Azure Blog as of June 8, 2026.
